column1: # runner-requirements.tsv: what a Linux bench or runner needs for the fleet's CI work, one requirement per line, checked
# by `nova-fleet audit` (audit.yml; cmd/nova-fleet/README.md, "audit") as the runner login, with the runner's PATH.
#   name     one word or a few, unique; what FLEET-AUDIT MISSING prints as item=
#   arch     where it applies: any, amd64 or arm64, or a comma list of them, with not-wsl to leave out WSL machines and
#            vm-tier to leave out a machine whose nova_runner_vm_kernel is false;
#            where it does not apply the audit prints FLEET-AUDIT NOT-APPLICABLE for it, never a silent skip
#   install  the play that installs it (runner-packages, sdk-toolchain, github-runners), or base: an essential package
#   check    a bash command, run with no input, that exits 0 when the requirement is met
# The pins (versions and sha256) are the ones the CI work checks for itself.

column4: command -v gcc && command -v g++ && command -v cc && command -v c++ && command -v make
command -v readelf && command -v nm && command -v ar

column1: # by path: the SDK puts its own cppcheck first on a runner's PATH, and the tidy gate names apt's (CPPCHECK=/usr/bin/cppcheck)

column4: v=$(go env GOVERSION) && printf '%s\n' go1.26.6 "$v" | sort -V -C && command -v gofmt

export PKG_CONFIG_LIBDIR=/usr/lib/s390x-linux-gnu/pkgconfig:/usr/share/pkgconfig && pkg-config --exists libsodium libbpf libxdp && test -e /usr/lib/s390x-linux-gnu/libsodium.so && test -e /usr/lib/s390x-linux-gnu/libbpf.so && test -e /usr/lib/s390x-linux-gnu/libxdp.so
(command -v qemu-s390x-static || command -v qemu-s390x) && command -v qemu-system-s390x && command -v qemu-img
command -v podman && command -v newuidmap && command -v newgidmap
command -v ssh && command -v scp && command -v ssh-keygen

command -v sha256sum && command -v sha512sum && command -v timeout && command -v setarch && command -v flock && command -v mountpoint && command -v dmesg && command -v getconf && command -v xargs && command -v awk && command -v tar && command -v sudo
